title: Rotate matrix 90 degrees (Python)
description: Rotating a square matrix clockwise equals transpose followed by reversing each row — zip(*m) transposes elegantly in Python.
how_it_works: Lab exercise: type the snippet into a fresh file, run it, and confirm the test outputs match. Then change one input and predict the result before running — Reversing rows then transposing maps element (r,c) to (c, n-1-r): a 90-degree clockwise turn.

test_cases.note: Determinism check: re-running the snippet reproduces the identical output.

pitfalls: Only square matrices rotate in place cleanly; rectangular ones change shape.
use_cases: Image rotation, game boards, matrix drills.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Rotate matrix 90 degrees (Python)
demo.program:
# JAH demo program — jahdb-demo-1.0
# Database: code-database · Record: JAH-CODE-0000006
# RUN: PC: save as demo.py, run `python3 demo.py`.

def rot(m):
    return [list(r) for r in zip(*m[::-1])]

print(rot([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]))
